─── Accessibility check (advisory — never blocks the build) ───

Found 5 things that would make this hard to use for some people (checked in 2 themes):

• 2 controls do not show where the keyboard is
     Why it matters: When someone moves through the page with the Tab key, nothing lights up, so they cannot tell which control they are on.
     What to do:     Add a visible outline (a focus ring) on the control itself when it is focused — not only on a box around it.

• 1 focus outline is too faint to see (2 places on the page)
     Why it matters: The control does light up when focused, but the outline is so close in colour to its background that a keyboard user still cannot tell where they are.
     What to do:     Make the focus outline stand out clearly — a stronger colour or a thicker ring, so it is at least three times the contrast of whatever is behind it.

• 1 component does not expose what its role requires
     Why it matters: The contract or a Figma note says what the component is (a toggle button, a checkbox, a text field, a tab). Assistive technology needs the matching wiring: the pressed or checked state, a label, the error link, the selected tab.
     What to do:     Add what the finding names (aria-pressed that changes on click, a real checkbox input with a label, aria-invalid and aria-describedby on an errored field, aria-selected on the selected tab, disabled or aria-disabled).

• 1 component does not render what its Figma accessibility note says
     Why it matters: A Figma annotation on the component states its role, name, heading level or alt text; the rendered page says something else.
     What to do:     Render what the annotation says, or update the annotation in Figma if the design changed.

Want the exact list? Run the same command again with --a11y — it shows every element and where to find it. (Add --json instead for a machine-readable version an agent can act on.)

Tip for a deeper check: this looked at "apps/gallery/ui.html", which only shows the components that happen to be on screen. For the most thorough check — every component in every state (normal, disabled, error, focused) — add a styleguide (one page that shows all your components). Once it exists, this check finds and uses it automatically, so nothing is missed.
